messages.subject: WLSMV estimator for multigroup confirmatory factor analysis
parts:
Hello,
I have categorical and not normal data and would like to run a multigroup CFA for three different age groups (young adults vs. adults vs. older adults). Since my data is not normal, I used the WLSMV estimator. 

I have two questions concerning the Lavaan output of the analysis: 1) If I want to do the CFA for each group separately with the WLSMV, what columns and rows do I look? Do I look the "DWLS" column or the "Robust" column? 2) Also, all of the robust fit indices (i.e. Robust CFI, Robust TLI and Robust RMSEA) are marked as NA while the non-robust ones, that is CFI, TLI and RMSEA seem excellent. What indices should I consider? The robust or the non-robust ones? Thank you for your responses!
Natalija

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: WLSMV estimator for multigroup confirmatory factor analysis
parts: 1) If I want to do the CFA for each group separately with the WLSMV, what columns and rows do I look?
You need to fit the model to each group separately, creating separate lavaan models.
Do I look the "DWLS" column or the "Robust" column?
Always the robust column.
2) Also, all of the robust fit indices (i.e. Robust CFI, Robust TLI and Robust RMSEA) are marked as NA

They are unavailable for scaled-shifted statistics, which is the robust correction used under WLSMV.  The "Robust" column contains the indices calculated using the robust chi-squared statistics.  They don't consistently estimate a population parameter, but I doubt they are quite far off in most cases.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
